title: Manual SQL Emulation in Loops vs Declarative Aggregates
pattern: Retrieving raw rows and iterating over them in application code to compute simple metrics (like sums or counts) instead of using declarative SQL aggregates.
why_bad: High memory and CPU cost. It drags thousands of records over the network to the application memory just to compute a single integer, wasting bandwidth and ignoring efficient database index scans [250, 538, 604].
detection: Application loops performing basic math (e.g., additions, counts) on lists of rows retrieved from a database query.
counterexample: Performing complex business logic or transformations on data that cannot be represented in SQL.
source:
*Implementing Domain-Driven Design (Vernon), p. 471 [250, 538]*  
*Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture (Fowler), p. 110 [604]*
